name: OnabotulinumtoxinA OAB dose-ranging trial
question: Which intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA dose balances urgency-incontinence improvement and voiding risk in idiopathic overactive bladder inadequately managed with anticholinergics?

design.population: Patients with idiopathic overactive bladder and urinary urgency incontinence inadequately managed with anticholinergics, with at least eight urgency-incontinence episodes weekly and eight micturitions daily at baseline.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose-ranging randomized trial
design.locator: Dmochowski PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00168454, Participant Flow, Started (arm counts)

verdictNote: Benefit began at 100 U; higher doses increased residual-volume and catheterization concerns.
takeaway: Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 50–300 U was compared with placebo for idiopathic overactive bladder with urgency incontinence. The week-12 report found sustained efficacy at doses of 100 U or greater, with dose-dependent postvoid residual and catheterization effects; its authors favored 100 U as a possible benefit–risk balance.

reports.label: Primary dose-ranging report
reports.citation: Dmochowski R, Chapple C, Nitti VW, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA for Idiopathic Overactive Bladder: A Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Randomized, Dose Ranging Trial." *J Urol.* 2010;184(6):2416-2422. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.08.021

results.measure: 7-day bladder-diary change from baseline at week 12
results.note: Abstract reports durable efficacy at doses of 100 U or greater without arm estimates or a prespecified testing threshold; doses above 150 U added minimal symptom benefit.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Significantly more frequent with onabotulinumtoxinA than placebo; rates not provided.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.note: Significantly more frequent with onabotulinumtoxinA than placebo; rates not provided.

harms.label: Postvoid residual and intermittent catheterization
harms.note: Both increased with dose; rates and catheterization thresholds not provided.

delivery.label: Treatment administration
delivery.value: Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 50, 100, 150, 200, or 300 U, or placebo; injection-site number and pattern not stated in abstract.

reports.label: Urodynamic analysis
reports.citation: Rovner E, Kennelly M, Schulte-Baukloh H, et al. "Urodynamic Results and Clinical Outcomes with Intradetrusor Injections of OnabotulinumtoxinA in a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Dose-Finding Study in Idiopathic Overactive Bladder." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2011;30(4):556-562. doi:10.1002/nau.21021

results.endpoint: Maximum cystometric capacity and volume at first involuntary detrusor contraction
results.note: Improvements generally decreased by week 36; no difference in clinical outcomes by baseline detrusor overactivity status was reported.

results.endpoint: No urgency urinary incontinence on diary
results.note: Active-dose range endpoints only are stated in the abstract; arm denominators come from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00168454 Participant Flow.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00168454, Participant Flow, Started

harms.label: Postvoid residual above 200 mL
harms.note: More common with doses above 150 U; arm rates not provided.

reports.label: Quality-of-life analysis
reports.citation: Fowler CJ, Auerbach S, Ginsberg D, et al. "OnabotulinumtoxinA Improves Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with Urinary Incontinence Due to Idiopathic Overactive Bladder: A 36-Week, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Randomized, Dose-Ranging Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2012;62(1):148-157. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.03.005
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Design, Setting, and Participants

results.measure: Change from baseline at weeks 2 through 24
results.note: Total and subscale scores; abstract does not give point estimates. Some quality-of-life measures were exploratory and unvalidated.
